title: Hollywood and Regional Hits Squeeze Bollywood's Share Below 40 Percent in 2026
excerpt: India's box office is headed for a record year, but Ormax data shows Hindi cinema ceding ground to a ₹500-crore Spider-Man and surging Telugu and Tamil releases.
body:
• India's domestic box office reached ₹8,147 crore through July 2026, up 13% year on year — but Hindi cinema's share has slipped below 40% for the first time this year, to 38%.
  • Hollywood's share hit a record 17%; Spider-Man: Brand New Day crossed ₹500 crore, the highest-grossing international film ever in India.
  • Telugu (18%), Tamil (13%) and Malayalam (7%) cinema now claim a combined 38% of domestic revenue — matching Hindi's entire share.
  • July's four biggest releases captured 81% of the month's collections, with Spider-Man alone taking 40%.

On paper, Indian cinema is enjoying one of its strongest commercial runs since the pandemic. Through the first seven months of 2026, cumulative gross domestic collections reached ₹8,147 crore — up 13% compared with the same period in 2025, according to Ormax Media data reported by CNBC TV18. July alone added ₹1,582 crore, the second-highest-grossing month of the year so far.

But beneath the record topline, the money is moving away from Mumbai. For the first time in 2026, Hindi cinema's share has slipped below 40%, settling at 38% through July — down from 44% at the end of June. The ground it lost has been captured by Hollywood spectacles and consistent regional blockbusters.

Hollywood's record run

International cinema was the primary disruptor in 2026, expanding to a record-high 17% share of domestic box-office revenue through July — Hollywood's previous annual best was 15% in 2019.

Driving the surge was Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which grossed over ₹500 crore — surpassing Avatar: The Way of Water to become the highest-grossing international film of all time in India, and the second-highest-grossing film of 2026 overall. It trails only Dhurandhar: The Revenge, which crossed the ₹1,000 crore mark domestically to become the highest-grossing Hindi film of all time. Alongside Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey (₹220 crore), international films generated over ₹1,424 crore through July — on track to eclipse Hollywood's 2019 India revenue record of ₹1,595 crore.

The regional surge

Telugu cinema currently commands an 18% share of the domestic box office, Tamil cinema holds 13%, and Malayalam and other regional languages account for 7% each — a combined 38%, equal to Hindi's entire share.

The shift shows up in the year's top titles. Across the top 10 domestic releases of 2026 through July, Hindi cinema accounts for four — Dhurandhar: The Revenge, Border 2, Bhooth Bangla and Dhamaal 4 — while Telugu (Peddi, Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu), Tamil (Jana Nayagan, Karuppu) and Hollywood (Spider-Man, The Odyssey) claim two spots each. Ormax's April data had Hindi at a 50% share; by July that lead had evaporated.

A two-tentpole economy

The strong headline hides a fragile structure. Ashish Misra, head of commercialisation at Cinepolis India, notes that Q1 2026's ₹3,440 crore — 17% higher than Q1 2025 — was shaped by "two large tentpoles at the bookends," while February, at under ₹500 crore, was the softest month since February 2023.

"The headline is strong, the curve underneath it is still uneven. That distinction matters because it tells us where the work still is."

— Ashish Misra, Head of Commercialisation, Cinepolis India

Misra identifies the missing middle as the real task: building "a steady flow of films in the ₹50 to ₹200 crore band that keep occupancy healthy week on week" between the tentpoles. July illustrates the concentration: the top four releases — Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the Tamil blockbuster Jana Nayagan (₹230 crore), The Odyssey (₹220 crore) and the Hindi comedy Dhamaal 4 (₹197 crore) — accounted for 81% of the month's receipts, with Spider-Man generating 40% on its own.

Impact and analysis

Hollywood franchises now open day-and-date with massive dubbed footprints, pulling the top end of the audience, while regional cinema — which recovered faster from the pandemic — eats the middle with pan-India dubbed releases. For Bollywood, the danger is not a bad year — 2026 is a record one — but a shrinking claim on it. When a single Hollywood title outgrosses every Hindi release of the month except the year's biggest, the centre of gravity has moved.

Diaspora angle

Overseas, diaspora audiences mirror the trend: Spider-Man: Brand New Day also reclaimed the No. 1 global box-office spot, while Telugu and Tamil blockbusters continue to fill North American multiplexes — the same screens where Hindi tentpoles once had the weekend to themselves.

What's next

The second half of 2026 is packed: Ramayana: Part 1, King, Toxic, Fauzi, Jailer 2 and Avengers: Doomsday. Ormax's first-half report put January-June at ₹6,398 crore — the strongest post-pandemic first half — and said 100 crore annual footfalls remain achievable. Whether Hindi cinema reclaims share will depend on the festival slate, not the record books.
